answer.policy_title: Medical Policy Manual – Surgery, Policy No. 187: Lumbar Spinal Fusion
answer.effective_date: Effective: July 1, 2026 (Last Review: March 2026; Next Review: October 2026)
criteria_quotes: MEDICAL POLICY CRITERIA Note: Clinical documentation to support criteria is required (See Required Documentation).

I. Lumbar spinal fusion may be considered medically necessary in individuals with any of the following conditions: A. Spinal fracture with instability or neural compression; or B. Spinal repair surgery for dislocation, tumor, or infection ... or C. Spinal stenosis when all of the following Criteria are met: 1. Neurogenic claudication or radicular pain; and 2. Documented central, lateral recess, or foraminal stenosis ... consistent with the individual's symptoms; and 3. Spondylolisthesis at a level (L1-S1) to be included in the fusion demonstrated on x-rays, CT, or MRI or there is a high likelihood of post-operative instability ...; and 4. There is either clinical documentation of significant functional impairment or disability, or objective measurement of severe disability using the Oswestry Disability Index tool; and 5. There is clinical documentation that a minimum of three months of conservative nonoperative therapy failed to adequately treat the individual's current symptoms including one or more of the following: a. Documented cauda equina syndrome, progressive motor loss, or subjective worsening of symptoms during a course of conservative management ... or b. All of the following Criteria are met: i. Physical therapy or professionally-directed therapeutic independent home exercise program unless contraindication is clearly documented; and ii. Two or more of the following treatment modalities have been attempted: ... anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics ... nerve membrane stabilizers or muscle relaxants ... acupuncture, chiropractic manipulation, massage therapy, yoga, meditation ... injection therapy (epidural steroid injection, medial branch block, radiofrequency ablation, selective nerve root injection, or discogram); and 6. The individual is nicotine-free OR there is clinical documentation that the individual has been abstinent from nicotine use for at least six weeks prior to planned procedure based on attestation or laboratory results (cotinine or nicotine levels); or ...

F. Isthmic spondylolisthesis when all of the following Criteria are met: 1. Either congenital (Wiltse type I) or acquired pars defect (Wiltse II), documented on x-ray; and 2. Persistent (daily) back pain, with or without neurogenic claudication or radicular pain; and 3. ... significant functional impairment or disability, or objective measurement of severe disability using the Oswestry Disability Index tool; and 4. ... minimum of three months of conservative nonoperative therapy failed ...; and 5. The individual is nicotine-free OR abstinent from nicotine use for at least six weeks prior to planned procedure ...

G. Recurrent same level central, foraminal, or lateral recess stenosis, or recurrent same level, disc herniation when all of the following Criteria are met: 1. Previous surgery was performed at least six months ago and resulted in significant interval relief of prior primary symptoms unless there is documented cauda equina syndrome, progressive motor loss, or subjective worsening of symptoms ...; and 2. Recent imaging consistent with signs and symptoms ...; and 3. ... significant functional impairment or disability, or objective ... Oswestry Disability Index ...; and 4. ... minimum of three months of conservative nonoperative therapy failed ...; and 5. Nicotine-free or documented abstinence for six weeks ...
answer.appeal_deadline: 180 days from the date of the notice (2026-08-07), i.e., must be received by 2027-02-03, as stated in the denial letter. This matches Regence's standard commercial/ACA member appeal window.
answer.submission_route: Per Regence's published Washington member appeal contacts (Parity Registry, sourced from Regence's own materials): call Regence Member Services at 800-365-3155, or submit a completed appeal form in writing to: Regence BlueCross BlueShield of Oregon, Attn: Regence Level 1 Member Appeals, PO Box 4208, Portland, OR 97208-4208. The specific appeal form should be obtained from regence.com/member/members/member-appeals or from the phone number/portal listed on the member's ID card, since the exact submission address/fax/portal can vary by exact plan and is best confirmed directly with Regence or in the denial notice's full appeal-rights section (which was not fully reproduced in the excerpt provided).
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The full SUR187 policy (11 pages) was retrieved directly from Regence's public medical policy PDF library (blue.regence.com/trgmedpol/surgery/sur187.pdf) and is also listed in Regence's provider-facing medical policy table of contents at regence.com/provider/library/policies-guidelines/medical-policy. The patient/provider can also request the exact clinical review criteria Regence applied to this specific denial by calling the customer service number on the back of the member ID card and asking for a copy of the medical policy/clinical review criteria cited in the denial (reference POC-A93FE7E3B5-95850), which is the patient's right under ACA/Washington appeal regulations.
answer.notes: I located and directly read Regence's own 'Lumbar Spinal Fusion' medical policy (SUR187), which explicitly lists CPT 22612 in its coding section and sets out detailed medical-necessity criteria (spinal stenosis, isthmic spondylolisthesis, adjacent segment degeneration, recurrent herniation/stenosis, deformity/scoliosis, fracture/infection/tumor pathways), each requiring documented conservative therapy, functional impairment/ODI scoring, imaging findings, and nicotine status. This is very likely the specific document referenced in the denial ('applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria'), because the denial reason ('documentation submitted was incomplete') directly maps to the extensive required-documentation elements (imaging, ODI, conservative care trial, nicotine status) in SUR187. However, I could not independently confirm from the denial letter itself, nor from a source specific to this member's exact plan document, that SUR187 (rather than a slightly different version/date) is the exact policy version cited by the reviewer — the policy PDF states an effective date of July 1, 2026, which is after the August 2026 denial date, so it is possible a slightly earlier version of the same numbered policy (SUR187) was in effect at the time of this specific determination; the patient/provider should confirm the exact version cited with Regence. Similarly, the appeal mailing address (PO Box 4208, Portland, OR) was sourced from a third-party parity-advocacy site's compilation of insurer contacts rather than a Regence-hosted appeals page I could directly verify with full mailing details, so this should be double-checked against the specific appeal instructions/back page of the actual denial letter or by calling Regence Member Services before mailing.

Date of notice: 2026-08-07
Member: Emerson Delgado
Member ID: W727121486
Plan: Regence BlueShield (Commercial/ACA), state of Washington

Dear Emerson,

We reviewed the prior authorization request submitted by your provider for the following service:

    Requested service: Lower back (lumbar) fusion
    Procedure code (CPT): 22612

After review, this request is DENIED. Reason for determination: the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity.

This determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. You have the right to appeal this decision. Your appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of this notice (by 2027-02-03).

Reference number: POC-A93FE7E3B5-95850
